enonce_markdown:
Choose the best answer.

If it rains tomorrow, we \_\_\_\_\_\_ the football match.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

First conditional: if + present simple, will + base verb (real future possibility).

### Solution

The condition ("it rains") is a real possibility in the future, so this is a first conditional: "if" + present simple, then "will" + base verb. **Answer: b.**

enonce_markdown:
Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.

If you heat ice, it (melt) \_\_\_\_\_\_.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Zero conditional: if + present simple, present simple (facts that are always true).

### Solution

A general truth or scientific fact uses the zero conditional: if + present simple, present simple. The answer is "melts".

enonce_markdown:
Choose the best answer.

If I were the headmaster of our school, I \_\_\_\_\_\_ a bigger library.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Second conditional: if + past simple (were), would + base verb (unreal or imaginary present).

### Solution

"If I were" describes an imaginary present situation, so this is a second conditional: "would" + base verb. "Will build" is first conditional and "would have built" is third conditional. **Answer: d.**

enonce_markdown:
Choose the best answer.

Ndongo missed the bus. If he \_\_\_\_\_\_ earlier, he would have arrived on time.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle (unreal past).

### Solution

The result clause "would have arrived" shows a third conditional about the past, so the if-clause needs the past perfect: "had left". **Answer: c.**

enonce_markdown:
Choose the best answer.

Unless you \_\_\_\_\_\_ harder, you will fail the mock examination.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Unless = if ... not. After unless the verb is affirmative; a first conditional uses the present simple in the if-clause.

### Solution

"Unless" already means "if ... not", so the verb stays affirmative and in the present simple: "Unless you work". "Don't work" would make a double negative. **Answer: a.**

enonce_markdown:
Choose the best answer.

Had the farmer sold his cocoa earlier, he \_\_\_\_\_\_ a better price.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Inversion in a third conditional: Had + subject + past participle = If + subject + had + past participle; the result clause uses would have + past participle.

### Solution

"Had the farmer sold" is an inverted third conditional (= If the farmer had sold). The result is an unreal past, so "would have" + past participle: "would have received". **Answer: c.**
